diagnostic_evidence.quote: L_{\pi,y_\star}(x,y) = A(\pi)x + B(\pi)y + c(\pi,y_\star).
The maximality result above hinges on the restriction that $A(\pi)$ and $B(\pi)$ are independent of $y_\star$.
Clearly $\pi$ is not in $\mathrm{F}$ for general $f$ and has the exact affine conditioning map $L_{y_\star}(x,y) = f(y_\star)y$.

issues.failure_explanation: The characterized F is maximal only for weakly observation-dependent maps, not for all maps allowed by Definition def:affine_cond_map. For example, take independent Y,Z uniform on [-1,1] and X=(1+Y^2)Z. The affine map (x,y)↦(1+y_star^2)y is exact, but the conditional variance (1+y_star^2)^2/3 varies with the observation, excluding this law from F by Proposition prop:char_weak_set. Thus the unrestricted maximality claim is false even for bounded, finite-moment laws.

failure_location.quote: Finally, we ask what the largest possible set of measures  \(\mathrm{F}\) is that any measure-dependent affine transport could be exact for. After characterizing  \(\mathrm{F}\), we prove that the set of measures \(\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}\) for which the EnKU achieves exact conditioning is almost maximal in the sense that  \(\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}\cup\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}\) with a small symmetry class \(\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the abstract and corresponding maximality summaries explicitly to weakly observation-dependent affine maps, and acknowledge that the unrestricted exactness class is strictly larger.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract's all-affine maximality claim is unsupported; the formally stated weak-dependence characterization remains unaffected.
issues.title: The abstract overstates maximality over unrestricted affine conditioning maps
issues.why_classification: The repair changes the central maximality quantifier and withdraws the advertised guarantee for the fully observation-dependent regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given a probability measure $\pi \in \Pp_2(\R^n\times \R^m)$ with finite second moments

issues.failure_explanation: Finite second moments do not justify a root-N covariance-estimation bound. For a symmetric scalar law with tail P(|X|>t) proportional to t^(-5/2), the covariance exists, but a single observation of size proportional to sqrt(N) produces an order-one sample-variance error on an event of probability proportional to N^(-1/4). Hence the expected absolute covariance error cannot be O(N^(-1/2)). Standard covariance CLT bounds require additional moment and, where relevant, dependence hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Central limit theorems connect the mean-field theory to the empirical reality through bounds of the form $\mathbb{E}\|\hat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm F} \;\propto\:N^{-1/2}$   for i.i.d. and certain non-i.i.d. settings

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State this auxiliary rate only under finite fourth moments and appropriate dependence assumptions, distinguishing those assumptions from the P2 assumptions of the exactness results.
issues.overall_effect: The stated finite-sample justification for the mean-field approximation does not cover the paper's full P2 setting.
issues.title: The covariance root-N claim lacks the necessary moment assumptions
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis repairs the auxiliary rate statement without changing the exactness theory or the numerical examples.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is a simple consequence of the fact that $X + BY$ is Gaussian and there is an affine transport map between any two non-singular Gaussians.

issues.failure_explanation: Take independent standard-normal scalar X,Y and prescribe B=2. Cov(X+2Y)=5 is nonsingular, while the posterior variance is 1. However, Var(AX+2Y+c)=A^2+4, so no A,c work. Transporting X+BY by a further linear map S changes both coefficients, producing SX+SBY rather than SX+BY.

failure_location.quote: For example, for every choice of $B$ (assuming $\Cov(X+BY)$ has full rank for all $y_\star$) there are $A$  and $c$ such that $L_{\pi,y_\star}(x,y)= A(\pi,y_\star)x + B(\pi,y_\star)y + c(\pi,y_\star)$ is exact.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Parameterize a preliminary combination X+DY and then transport it, making clear that the final coefficients are A=S and B=SD; alternatively, restrict prescribed B to those satisfying the covariance feasibility condition.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed freedom to prescribe the final coefficient B is false, although Gaussian nonuniqueness itself remains valid.
issues.title: An arbitrary prescribed observation coefficient need not admit a Gaussian-exact map
issues.why_classification: The repair withdraws the substantive arbitrary-B promise, while retaining a comparable construction of multiple Gaussian-exact maps.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $Z_{\mathrm{cyc}} =(v_1^\top Z, v_2^\top Z)^\top$ satisfies cyclic symmetry of some order $k \in \N_{\geq 2}$
If $\pi \not \in \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cyc}}$, then $A$ has no complex eigenvalues with $|\lambda| = 1$ and  $\lambda \neq 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem gives necessary conditions for alternatives, not a converse. For a counterexample, let Y be standard Gaussian in R^2 and let independent Z assign masses 0.4,0.1,0.1,0.2,0.2 to (0,0),(-1,0),(1,1),(-2,1),(2,4), respectively; set X=Z+Y. The first coordinate of Z is symmetric, so taking v1=v2=e1 puts the law in S_cyc. Nevertheless, an exact map must have A+B=0, since otherwise its output has a nontrivial Gaussian component rather than finite support. The unique mass-0.4 atom fixes the translation. Preserving the mass-0.1 pair either forces A=I or swaps that pair; the swapping matrix sends (-2,1) to (2,3), which is not in the support. Thus only the EnKU is exact.

failure_location.quote: While by $\pi \in \mathrm{E}^\mathrm{EnKU}$ the EnKF is exact on each of these symmetry classes, the proof of the following theorem reveals that there are many other affine conditioning maps that are also exact.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe these classes as containing possible exceptions to uniqueness, and restrict affirmative nonuniqueness claims to cases where an actual symmetry or decomposition of the full residual law yields another map.
issues.overall_effect: The symmetry classes cannot be interpreted as sufficient conditions for multiple exact updates. The theorem and its uniqueness corollary retain their stated one-way implications.
issues.title: Membership in a projected symmetry class does not guarantee nonuniqueness
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening repairs the interpretation, but the asserted converse cannot be retained for the defined projection-based classes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider $\pi \in \mathrm{E}^\mathrm{EnKU}$ with non-singular covariance $\Sigma_{YY}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Let n=m=1, Y=0 almost surely, and X=Z be Bernoulli with parameter strictly between 0 and 1 but different from 1/2. This law belongs to E^EnKU and to none of the three listed symmetry classes: Z has positive variance, is not centrally symmetric, and cannot have the stated decomposition driven by the constant Y. Yet every map ell_b(x,y)=x+by is exact for the chosen conditional kernel. These are distinct affine maps, whereas the EnKU is x.

failure_location.quote: The previous section established that, apart from a small symmetry class $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cov}} \cup \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{dec}}  \cup \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cyc}} $, the Ensemble Kalman Update (EnKU) is the unique affine conditioning map that is exact for any element  $\pi \in\mathrm{E}^\mathrm{EnKU}$ and observation $y_\star\in\R^m$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the nonsingularity assumption into the summaries, or state uniqueness only modulo agreement on the affine support of the joint, using the projection reduction already discussed in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: Literal uniqueness as a map on the whole input space fails in singular observation directions; the correctly qualified corollary is unaffected.
issues.title: The uniqueness summary omits the nonsingular observation-covariance condition
issues.why_classification: This is a local qualification of irrelevant off-support freedom, with a source-supported projection repair and no loss of the distributional update guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Within $\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$, each of the symmetry classes above carves out a highly non-generic and (topologically speaking) small subset of laws.
\mathrm{F} = \mathrm{E}^\mathrm{EnKU} \cup \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}.

The theorem is proved in the appendix and shows that weak $y_\star$–dependence leaves essentially no room to beat the EnKU: the maximal exact set collapses to $\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$ up to the narrow class $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: An existential decomposition identity does not establish topological smallness, and the paper supplies no size criterion or proof. Moreover, let Y be uniform on [-1,1] and X=Y^2. This law is in F via the weakly dependent map ell(x,y)=y_star^2, but is not in E^EnKU because K=0. Near any law with positive Var(Y), E^EnKU is W2-closed: covariance continuity gives convergence of K, and independence of X-KY and Y is preserved under the resulting limits. Consequently a neighborhood of this law relative to F is disjoint from E^EnKU and, by the stated decomposition, lies in S_nl-dec. Thus E^EnKU is not even dense in F, and the exception need not be nowhere dense there.

failure_location.quote: This class is “small’’ in the same sense as our earlier symmetry classes—it is defined by  invariance/identities (e.g., a generalized $\lambda$–decomposition tying a one–dimensional nonlinear feature of the $Y$–marginal to a linear functional of $Z$).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the structural decomposition while withdrawing the unsupported smallness and near-maximality interpretations. Any stronger replacement must specify a size notion and establish it on an explicitly restricted class.
issues.overall_effect: The structural set equality survives, but it does not establish the advertised topological genericity, negligible enlargement, or size-based near-optimality.
issues.title: The exceptional class is not shown to be small and can contain relatively open parts of F
issues.why_classification: The advertised generic near-maximality interpretation cannot be recovered by a local omitted argument: the natural relative-topological interpretation has a counterexample, so a substantive promise must be abandoned or replaced.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider any measure $r \in \Pp(\R)$ and measurable function $f:\R\rightarrow \R$.
\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m)\times\mathbb{R}^m

issues.failure_explanation: The construction allows arbitrary probability laws and arbitrary measurable f, whereas affine conditioning maps in the paper accept only P2 joints. Even with r standard normal, choosing f(y)=exp(y^2) makes E[(f(Y)Z)^2] infinite for independent Y,Z with law r. The resulting joint is outside the declared domain, so the example's universal input contract is invalid.

failure_location.quote: Clearly $\pi$ is not in $\mathrm{F}$ for general $f$ and has the exact affine conditioning map $L_{y_\star}(x,y) = f(y_\star)y$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require r to have a finite second moment and f to belong to L2(r), or directly require the constructed joint to lie in P2.
issues.overall_effect: The example does not define a conditioning-map instance in the paper's framework for all of its stated inputs.
issues.title: The observation-dependent example can leave the stated P2 domain
issues.why_classification: A local integrability condition restores the existing domain and preserves the bounded examples demonstrating enlargement beyond F.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the analysis maps are chosen as  $L_{\pi, y_\star}(x,y) =x + B(\pi, y_\star) y+ c(\pi, y_\star)$

issues.failure_explanation: For the displayed learned-filter family A=I, varying B with the observation cannot enlarge E^EnKU. Let K=Cov(X,Y)Cov(Y)^dagger and h(Y)=E[X|Y]-EX-K(Y-EY). Exactness almost surely in the observation, together with total covariance, gives 0=E[(B(Y)+K)Cov(Y)(B(Y)+K)^T]+Cov(h(Y)). Both terms are positive semidefinite, so both vanish. Thus B(y) agrees with -K on the covariance range and the conditional mean is affine; matching means then makes the update distribution exactly the EnKU distribution. The broader examples with A different from I do not justify the claimed exactness enlargement for the learned gain-only form.

failure_location.quote: In that sense, our negative result in Theorem \ref{thm:F_char} for weakly $y_\star$–dependent maps helps understand why learned methods pursue $y_\star$–dependent updates: without such dependence, there is essentially no headroom beyond EnKU, whereas allowing dependencies of $B(y_\star)$ on $y_\star$ could potentially realize exact updates for broader constructions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Separate approximation improvements from enlargement of the exactness class. State that the displayed A=I family has no larger exactness class, and attribute the broader constructions to allowing different state coefficients A.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed exactness-based explanation for observation-dependent learned gains is misleading, although the general observation-dependent examples remain valid after their moment qualification.
issues.title: Observation-dependent gains alone cannot enlarge exactness when A equals I
issues.why_classification: A contained covariance argument and a limited revision of the learned-filter interpretation suffice; the general affine characterization need not be rebuilt.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We condition on the fixed observation $y_\star=(0.4,-0.2)^\top$ and compare several affine conditioning maps as the ensemble size $N$ increases, reporting the $W_2$-distance between the analysis ensemble and the true posterior.

Importantly, our analysis is mean-field and {does not model} many practical effects—localization, covariance inflation, finite-$N$ sampling error, model error/mis-specification, and adaptive tuning—which are known to strongly impact performance.

issues.failure_explanation: Exactness removes population bias but supplies no empirical W2 rate. For a concrete counterexample to this inference, take constant Y and Bernoulli X. EnKU is exactly the identity, all moments are finite, and if p_N is the empirical Bernoulli weight then W2^2=|p_N-p|. Consequently the expected W2 error is of order N^(-1/4), not N^(-1/2). The paper gives no separate empirical-transport analysis establishing the asserted rate for its continuous two-dimensional examples either.

failure_location.quote: Since the EnKU is exact for these distributions in the mean field, we expect its error to decrease with $N$ to $0$ at a parametric rate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the parametric-rate assertion and retain a qualitative consistency expectation, or provide a metric-specific finite-sample analysis accounting for empirical transport and gain-estimation errors.
issues.overall_effect: The parametric-rate prediction is not established by the mean-field results or by covariance estimation rates; qualitative bias-floor comparisons remain separate.
issues.title: Mean-field exactness does not imply a parametric empirical Wasserstein rate
issues.why_classification: Repair requires either a nontrivial finite-sample argument or withdrawal of the quantitative rate claim, while leaving the static exactness theory intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $Y = HX + \xi$ with linear $H$,  independent mean-zero $\xi$, and  $\text{Cov}(\xi) = \Gamma$ finite.
$(\hat X_f^{(c)})^\top H^\top\Gamma^{-1} H\hat X_f^{(c)}= C D C^T$

issues.failure_explanation: A finite covariance is only positive semidefinite. The stated assumptions permit, for example, H=0 and Gamma=0, making the inverse in C_a undefined. The later A^(3) construction additionally uses Gamma^(-1), which can be undefined even when H C_f H^T+Gamma is invertible.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume Gamma is positive definite for these standard ESRF formulas, or supply a separate support-aware pseudoinverse treatment for singular observation noise.
issues.overall_effect: The inverse-based ESRF procedures are not defined on all inputs admitted by the appendix's assumptions.
issues.title: The ESRF constructions use inverses without an invertibility hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard local positive-definiteness hypothesis repairs this auxiliary derivation without changing the paper's pseudoinverse-based EnKU results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \hat C_f := \frac{1}{N-1}\hat X_f \left(I_N - \frac{1}{N}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top\right)\hat X_f^\top
$\hat X_f^{(c)} = \hat X_f \left(I_N - \frac{1}{N}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top\right)$
$(\hat X_f^{(c)})^\top H^\top\Gamma^{-1} H\hat X_f^{(c)}= C D C^T$

issues.failure_explanation: The anomaly matrix is unnormalized. Therefore the displayed transform produces covariance C_f-(N-1)C_f H^T S^(-1)H C_f, where S=H C_f H^T+Gamma, instead of the stated C_a. Its right-hand side need not even be positive semidefinite: with scalar C_f=H=Gamma=1 and N=4, the rank-one subtraction has eigenvalue 3/2. The corresponding Gram matrix defining D for A^(3) likewise lacks the factor 1/(N-1).

failure_location.quote: \hat T \hat T ^\top  =  I_N - \left(\hat X_f^{(c)}\right)^\top H^\top\left(H\hat C_fH^\top + \Gamma\right)^{-1}H\hat X_f^{(c)}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert 1/(N-1) in the linear-model transform covariance and its square-root formula, and normalize the Gram matrix defining D consistently. The later joint-sample projection formula T' does not require this extra factor.
issues.overall_effect: The stated ETKF square root can fail to exist and does not generally meet the analysis-covariance condition; the same normalization error affects A^(3).
issues.title: The linear-model ensemble transforms omit the covariance normalization
issues.why_classification: Consistent local covariance normalization repairs the formulas and preserves all intended methods and moment guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\hat X_f^{(c)} = F G U^T$ is the SVD  and $(\hat X_f^{(c)})^\top H^\top\Gamma^{-1} H\hat X_f^{(c)}= C D C^T$  is the eigenvalue decomposition  with the eigenvectors in the null space  arranged as the final columns of \(C\).
\hat A \hat C_f\hat A^\top = \hat C_a.

issues.failure_explanation: Ordering zero eigenvalues last does not distinguish the null space of H X_f^(c) from the smaller null space of X_f^(c), and G^dagger selects coordinates according to the latter rank. For example, take n=1, N=2, X_f^(c)=(1,-1), H=0, Gamma=1, F=1, G=(sqrt(2),0), and the allowed eigendecomposition C=I, D=0. The formula gives A^(3)=1/sqrt(2), reducing covariance from 2 to 1 although C_a=C_f=2. Since N-1=1 and Gamma is positive definite, this defect survives both preceding repairs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: With r=rank(X_f^(c)), require the first r columns of C to span the row space of X_f^(c), diagonalizing the Gram matrix there, and take the remaining columns in ker(X_f^(c)).
issues.overall_effect: A permitted eigendecomposition can corrupt the analysis covariance even in the no-observation case.
issues.title: The A^(3) formula requires an additional null-space alignment rule
issues.why_classification: The already computed SVD supplies this local null-space alignment, so an explicit eigenbasis rule restores the guarantee without restricting the observation model.
